doc: Authored tail centrelines for tools/rig_meshy_tail.py (decision 0191). Points are bind-pose metres in glTF axes (+Y up, +Z front), root first. radius is the capsule that bounds the surface walk from the tail tip. Validated against rendered segmentation plots, 2026-09-26.

spring.tested: not in the demo; copied from mouse_keeper
not in the demo; copied from otter_boatwright

no_chain.mole_digger: No tail separable from the body in the 2026-09-26 bind-pose plots. The DEC-039 landmarks give moles a 120 permille stub (~0.11 m), which can ride the hips.
no_chain.mole_mason: No tail separable from the body in the 2026-09-26 bind-pose plots; same 120 permille stub landmark as mole_digger.
no_chain.badger_cellarer: No tail separable in the 2026-09-26 bind-pose plots; the long tunic covers the seat.
no_chain.badger_quarryman: No tail separable in the 2026-09-26 bind-pose plots.
no_chain.badger_steward: Not rigged at all: the robe defeated Meshy's auto-rigger (decision 0188).

spring_units: Godot 4.7 SpringBoneSimulator3D: gravity in m/s^2 and radius in metres, in WORLD units -- not the skeleton's local units, although the skeleton sits under the glTF's 0.01-scale armature. Verified 2026-09-26: scaling both by 100 collapsed the squirrel forester's tail and lifted the otter's.
